headline: Three futures for 2030: optimistic, base, downside
definition: Optimistic = the carriers' view: a tight market with little overcapacity

fan.label: Median gap at the peak: 5.98 M TEU of deliveries land in 2028 (Alphaliner)
fan.note: Band = P10 to P90 of 5,000 runs. Gap above zero: supply grows faster than demand.
fan.insight: The utilisation index stays near 77 even when the gap closes: the overhang does not go away, it just stops growing.

scenarios.name: Optimistic
scenarios.story: Demand runs about 1.2 pp a year above Drewry’s path and a share of deliveries slips: the gap is back to about zero by 2030.
scenarios.act: Hold newbuild slots back, add no new orders, keep scrapping steady.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.story: Demand follows Drewry, about 12% of deliveries slip and 2.2 M TEU are scrapped over 2027 to 2030: the gap peaks near +14 in 2028 and is +1.4 in 2030.
scenarios.act: Blank sailings and slow steaming to protect rates, scrap the oldest ships.

scenarios.name: Downside
scenarios.story: Demand runs about 1.2 pp a year below Drewry and little scrapping happens: overcapacity is still +2.9 pp in 2030.
scenarios.act: Deeper blank sailings, scrap beyond the 0.655 M TEU record (needs yards) and consolidate.

spread: The three paths differ mostly in demand (about 1.2 pp a year either way). The year Suez returns barely separates them.
signposts: Demand against Drewry’s +4.2% for 2027: the biggest swing between our three paths.
Ships still on Cape routes (about 250 in Sep 2026, Linerlytica): a quick fall means Suez capacity returns early.
Scrapping against about 0.3 M TEU in 2027 (2025 actual: 0.008, record: 0.655).
Slippage and new orders after Oct 2026, ahead of the 5.98 M TEU due in 2028.
limits: Not modelled: Hormuz closure, port congestion, slow steaming, consolidation.
Ranges are our own estimates: the fan is a simulation, not a forecast.
Scenarios are the median of the runs around P10, P50 and P90 of the 2030 utilisation index.
